solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient singer's awkward lack of flexibility

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: An elderly vocalist stubbornly refuses to change their repertoire.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigence is stubborn refusal to compromise, the exact opposite of being flexible.

clue.text: Fire, one not likely to engulf plant

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the plant sits inside the phrase before it

parts.note: the emphatic refusal 'Not likely!' means no
a fern is a leafy plant

explanation.surface: A fire that probably won't spread to the garden plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not likely!' is an informal way of saying no, which the solver may not think of as a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, fierce blaze, so it is a kind of fire.

clue.text: Business in the centre of Monterey is excellent for surfers

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits between its letters
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle pair of the eight letters is kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of an eight-letter name
rad is surfer slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A Californian surf town where the waves suit the local trade.
explanation.walkthrough: RAD sits between T and E: T(RAD)E. Monterey is a coastal town in California, which suits the surfer slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade means commerce or buying and selling, which is what business is.

clue.text: Spoiled cats fed duck in Berkshire town

indicators.note: being fed means taking something inside, so the duck goes into the jumble
spoiled means messed up, so the word after it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Pampered cats being given duck to eat in a smart English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot, in the English county of Berkshire, is famous for its royal horse-racing meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a town in Berkshire, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Drop off spades and planks

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
lumber is timber sawn into planks

explanation.surface: A tired gardener nods off beside the spades and planks in the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep, and to slumber is to sleep.

clue.text: Environmentalist and old nurse adopting horse — colt

indicators.note: adopting means taking something on, so the horse is attached in front of the old nurse

parts.note: a Green is a campaigner for the environment
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
O is the abbreviation for old
RN stands for Registered Nurse

explanation.surface: A campaigner and a retired nurse taking in a horse and its foal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' looks like part of the horse picture, but it is the definition in its sense of a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt can mean an inexperienced newcomer, and a greenhorn is a raw novice.

clue.text: Big heron flying around university, one located nearby

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumble wraps the university
something flying is moving about wildly, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A large wading bird circling a campus, perched somewhere close by.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is a person who lives next door or close at hand.

clue.text: Tasteful short song by a new talent at last

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the song word goes

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful song or poem
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of talent

explanation.surface: A brief, refined song performed by a promising new artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish, which is what tasteful describes.

clue.text: Old king's innards finally cut out

indicators.note: the final letter is cut out, leaving all the rest

parts.note: offal is the edible internal organs of an animal

explanation.surface: A medieval monarch's entrails are at last removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was the eighth-century king of Mercia, remembered for Offa's Dyke on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia over twelve centuries ago, an old king indeed.

clue.text: Burned with desire returning after date, say

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the sound-alike piece
say asks us to take the word as spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to date someone is to court them; in non-rhotic speech court rhymes with the start of cauterise

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word before it is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: Someone smitten again after a romantic evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burned with desire' reads as one phrase of passion, but 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cauterise a wound is to seal it by burning, so cauterised means burned in the medical sense.

clue.text: Burning Man's located east of old city

indicators.note: in an across clue east is to the right, so the man comes after the city

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: Directions to the Burning Man festival in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Burning Man is an American desert festival, which makes the first two words read as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A burning issue is a pressing one, so burning and urgent are synonyms.

clue.text: British individual had consumed drug — dope

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so the drug goes into the word before it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
an individual is one person
taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Briton who took drugs is called a dope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like more drug talk, but it is the definition: a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and a bonehead is a slang term for an idiot.

clue.text: Show-off behind comedy writer

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the show-off is placed last

parts.note: com is the shortening of comedy in sitcom and romcom
a poser is someone who shows off

explanation.surface: A boastful person standing behind a comedy writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comedy writer' reads as one job, but the definition is writer alone, here a writer of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music, so is a writer of scores.

clue.text: Sailor at sea, a pervert, pinches yours truly

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip, so the jumble closes round the speaker
at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
yours truly is the writer, I

explanation.surface: A creep on a ship grabs the narrator.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a sailor licensed by a government to attack enemy ships, a kind of legal pirate.

clue.text: Cloud the issue when one is thrown?

definitions.text: Cloud the issue when one is thrown?

parts.note: surface reading: muddy an argument so that nobody can see the point
setter's reading: a device hurled to give off a dense cloud of vapour

explanation.surface: Someone confusing a debate whenever they are caught off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' suggests being disconcerted, and 'cloud the issue' an evasive tactic; read literally, the thing thrown makes a real cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The device is lobbed to release a screen of vapour, literally clouding things.

clue.text: Troop travelling round Iberian city

indicators.note: travelling means on the move, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a round shape is like the letter O

explanation.surface: Soldiers on a tour around a Spanish or Portuguese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto, also called Porto, is a major city in Portugal, on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: All-purpose skimobile carrying Alaskan, perhaps?

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the answer is held inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A snowmobile for all uses transporting someone from Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous peoples of Alaska have been called Eskimo, so an Alaskan may be one, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Reportedly 2 in 20, say? That's greedy

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: 2 is TRADE and 20 is BLOATERS, which are an example of fish, so trade in them means sell fish

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle that ends by calling someone greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers refer to other answers: trade in bloaters is to sell fish, which spoken aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selfish puts their own wants first, which is what greedy describes.

clue.text: Band reportedly travelled on bypass

parts.note: a ring is a band, as on a finger

indicators.note: reportedly means as it would be heard, so the next word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: rode is the past tense of ride; its sound-alike is spelt differently

explanation.surface: A pop group said to have driven along the bypass on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring road is the British term for a road circling a town to avoid its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a road built to route traffic around a town, the same thing as a ring road.

clue.text: Martin is sorry about taking part in 12

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards
taking part in means being included within, so the answer lies inside the words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word to the middle of the last

explanation.surface: Martin apologises for his role in something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference 12, whose answer is COMPOSER; Rossini wrote The Barber of Seville.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was an Italian opera composer, so he is an example of the definition.

clue.text: A master's animation is stunning

parts.note: taken as written
MA is a Master of Arts degree
zing is liveliness or energy

explanation.surface: Praise for an expert animator's impressive cartoon work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animation' looks like cartoons, but here it means vivacity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amazing astonishes you, just as something stunning does.

clue.text: Lobster prepared with a smoked herring

definitions.note: herring is a noun whose plural is often the same as its singular, so smoked herring can stand for many fish and match a plural answer

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seafood platter of lobster served alongside kippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are whole herrings, lightly salted and cold-smoked, so they are smoked herring.

clue.text: Shock that's put on by 80s band in audition in tent

parts.note: a shock is a mass of hair, and one that is put on is a wig

indicators.note: an audition is something heard, so the band name is taken by sound

parts.note: Wham! was the 1980s pop duo of George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley

explanation.surface: A musician tries out for an 80s group while wearing a hairpiece inside a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a domed Native American dwelling, a type of tent.

clue.text: At which point, that woman comes between you and me

indicators.note: coming between means being set inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: you and I together are we
her refers to a particular woman

explanation.surface: Someone describes the moment another woman came between a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Where can ask or mean at what place or stage, which matches at which point.

clue.text: Boss detailed mistake

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with its tail, the final letter, removed

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A manager itemised an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'described closely' but is split as de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing error.

clue.text: 16:51 of a workday?

parts.note: surface reading: a precise clock time late in the afternoon
setter's reading: the time described as minutes before the hour, and also the usual office hours

explanation.surface: A timestamp near the end of the office day.
explanation.walkthrough: 16:51 is nine minutes before five in the afternoon; the same phrase names the standard office day from morning until evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the conventional name for regular office hours, as well as telling this time.

clue.text: Get angry following backchat

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lip is cheeky talk, insolence

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper after being answered back.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is informal for suddenly losing one's temper.

clue.text: Tough chap's snack

parts.note: hard-boiled describes a tough, unsentimental person
egg is old slang for a chap, as in a good egg

explanation.surface: A rugged man's light bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough chap' reads as one hard man; it splits into two pieces. 'Good egg' is British slang for a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg boiled until firm is a common portable snack.
